author: Horsfield, 1821

art.subject: Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo (Surniculus lugubris), adult: plumage entirely black with a blue-green gloss; a small white patch on the nape, often hidden; undertail coverts barred white; the outer tail feathers barred white on their undersides. Bill black, slender and slightly decurved; legs short and dark.
art.pose: perched upright on a branch in the mid-canopy, side view
art.scene: Broadleaf woodland edge on a Korean offshore island in May, during spring migration, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Slim, drongo-like cuckoo, a little smaller than Black Drongo, perching upright in the mid-canopy. Bill short, slender and slightly decurved, without the heavy hooked tip and bristles of a drongo. Legs short, with two toes forward and two back. Tail long and square-ended. Wings pointed; flight direct and cuckoo-like.
avoid: Do not paint a deeply forked tail; that marks Black Drongo and Fork-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo.
Do not paint a thick, hooked drongo bill; the bill is thin and slightly curved like a cuckoo's.
Do not omit the white bars under the tail.
Do not paint white spots on the body of the adult; spotting belongs to juveniles.
